statement: Declarative definitions of observable properties (I-ADOPT: property + object of interest + constraints; VIM: measurand vs influence quantity; LOINC: basis/time aspect as identity). One definition is consumed by reading (plan), interpretation (contract slots), attribution (which property a value reports) and evaluation (which conditions decide comparability). Properties and condition dimensions are shared across product categories; a category profile only says which properties apply and which conditions DEFINE the measurand there. Quantity kinds, metrics and units come from the quantity-knowledge pack. Written in PEE's own words; no third-party text reproduced. Every entry carries a lifecycle state (candidate | supported | verified | decision_usable) and its sources. A condition may define the measurand only for one basis (onlyForBasis): the usage pattern defines a periodic figure, not a per-run one. Attribution: a unit kind alone attributes only when the category profile lists exactly one property admitting it (the profile licenses it); otherwise a definition term must support the choice. A definition may name its object nouns (I-ADOPT object of interest); a candidate surface term supports the property only when one of them is present. Outside the categories whose profile lists a property, the value's own words must name the property's object (object nouns); inside them the category supplies the object. A property may declare a plausible SI range (plausibleSi; s, m, Pa, Hz, m3/s, dB): a value outside it is not attributed (SHACL-style value constraint). Object nouns name the measured object (acoustic output, audio path, obstacle), never the product class. A property may subsume QK metrics (relatedMetrics): those are not competing concepts.

basisCues.note: Words that STATE the basis (LOINC time aspect) of an extensive value; a unit may state it too (QK kinds energy_per_event, periodic_*). runNamed: words that name a run, programme or task, which license a definition's default per_run basis as an inferred (indefinite null instantiation) slot. A 'per' followed within two words by a runNamed word (per completed task) states per_run.

nonQkUnitForms.note: Unit classes the quantity-knowledge pack does not hold (S88 gap, recorded): currency and currency per energy. A currency form followed by a period (GBP/yr, £ per year) is currency with a per_period basis.

history.note: air purifiers and dishwashers (development); S88 fix1

S88 E4: robot floor cleaners and soundbars authored from owner packages 05 and 08 (supplement 01 only) BEFORE any document of these categories was read in S88; hash-sealed in evaluation/s88/e4-definitions-freeze.json

S89 (owner review of S88): known objects (I-ADOPT object of interest: a value naming another concept's object is not this property's) and plausible SI ranges (SHACL-style value constraints); profile licence removed by default

S90 (owner review of S89): document sections as knowledge (which headings announce specifications, the publisher's own tests, comparisons or quoted sources); the evidence role of a value is inherited from its structure first
S91 (owner review of S90): measurement cues as data (observation verbs); the evidence role comes from positive evidence for each class, never from a default

S98 (owner decision 2026-10-20): known objects may state the QK metrics whose object of interest they are (I-ADOPT object stated, never inferred from a name). 'display' is the object of the five display metrics (peak luminance, refresh rate, input lag, colour gamut coverage, colour error), which are display metrics by their QK definition. The S89 note 'not the object of any defined property' becomes a derived condition: a known object owned by a loaded definition is that definition's object, not another concept's.

S99 (owner review of S98, 2026-10-20): statementRoles (norm and target cues of a value's clause) so that a value a standard or a test target states is never read as the product's result; bounds come from the shared quantity-knowledge bound words.

S100 (owner review of S99, rule governance): reference nouns for the value-scope reference relation; threshold and norm cue lists no longer duplicate the quantity knowledge's bound words or name judgements (rule audit findings F2, F3). Statement roles are decided by the observation_semantics rules, not by cue order.

S100 development (spent S89-S99 material): 'performance', 'battery life' and 'noise' name aspects, not tests; as section words they announced a publisher test over declared values (12 of 26 section-decided roles wrong). They no longer count as test headings.

S102 (rule-ownership audit, lost-attribution census): 'spec', 'data sheet', 'datasheet', 'technical data' and 'technical details' announce a specification section (headings such as 'Spec:', 'Product spec:' and 'Data sheet <product>' were not recognised, so 19 declared values abstained). General section vocabulary, no page rule. 'when measuring' and 'while measuring' report the publisher's measurement (evidenceCues.measurement).

knownObjects.note: Objects that are not the object of any defined property but recur next to numbers. A value whose own words name one of them, and none of the candidate property's object nouns, is not attributed to that property (it may belong to an undefined concept, which stays unknown). S98: an object may state the QK metrics it is the object of (metrics); a definition of such a metric then owns the object, and the block applies only to the definitions that do not.

documentSections.note: Words in a section heading that announce what the section's values are. A value in a specification section is a declaration unless its own sentence states a measurement; a value in a test section is the publisher's own result unless its sentence states otherwise. Document structure, not property knowledge; kept as data so a correction propagates.

evidenceCues.note: Provenance cues in the value's own clause. A clause that attributes a capability or component to the product (has, equipped with, boasts, rated) without a measuring verb describes a specification (a declaration); measuring verbs are the S86c classifier's. Only applied when the sentence classifier found no other role. Measurement cues: verbs that report what the product did in use (lasted, completed, maxed); combined with the instrument dimension and the document's own testing they are positive evidence of an original measurement.

statementRoles.note: S99 (owner review 2026-10-20, verbatim in owner-review-s98-semantic-integrity-2026-10-20.md): the role of the statement a value sits in, decided before the value is attributed to a product. A measured quantity value (VIM 2.10) is not a specification limit or a maximum permissible value (VIM 4.26): a value a standard, regulation or guideline sets (norm) and a value a test or a buyer aims at (target) are never the product's result. Cues are matched in the value's own clause only. A bound ('under 45 dB', 'at least 30 cm') comes from the quantity knowledge's bound words (shared with request requirements). Words that state a recommendation about the product itself ('recommended room size') are deliberately absent: they describe the product, not a norm. pd.7 rev (S99 dev it2): norm cues are phrases that name an external rule ('the standard', 'requirements', 'a guideline'), never when a mode, setting or level word follows ('standard mode'); a bounded value with positive evidence of a result or specification is a bounded result or specification of the product, and a threshold is a bound in a generic or sufficiency claim ('anything under 45 dB', 'quiet enough'). pd.8 (S100 rule audit): a value that modifies a reference noun ('the 44 dB standard', 'the 80-decibel mark') is that reference (referenceNouns: norm or threshold), read at value scope; 'or less/or more' are bound words of the quantity knowledge, not threshold cues, and 'is considered'/'counts as' state a judgement, not a norm.
